cards.title: Method Selection and Validation Boundaries
cards.claim: Allometry and IVIVE require different inputs and binding conventions. Allometry is empirical and relies on cross-species similarity; IVIVE is mechanistic and relies on in vitro metabolic stability. Neither method is universally superior. A calibrated one-/two-species approach has method-specific evidence, but this does not authorize arbitrary fixed exponents. A validated human prediction cannot be established solely from good animal regression fit (R2). Human predictions are prospective scenarios; generic published human methodological examples are not observations for the target drug.
conditions: Project must specify which method is being applied and why.
Method-specific correction factors or external calibration evidence must be justified.
Do not treat a project-designed summary as a quoted regulatory requirement.
required_inputs: Explicit method specification for the target drug.
Evidence of method applicability to the target drug's chemical/mechanistic domain.
Distinction between animal internal checks and human validation.
limitations: A calibration coefficient from one drug is not transferable to every drug.
Abstract-only material supports only what appears in the abstract.
PDF text extraction does not inspect figures or validate table layout.
cards.downstream_use: Use to justify the selection of a translation method in the project plan. Document gaps in method qualification. Do not execute numerical workflows based on this card alone.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Allometry versus IVIVE: inputs, qualification and species limitations

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
